title: CX Connect at SAP Connect Las Vegas 2026: Turning Learning into Experience
author: FernandoRedondo
text:
As we reflect on our time at SAP Connect Las Vegas 2026 , one theme stands out above all else: meaningful engagement. Beyond presentations and product discussions, the event gave participants the opportunity to gain hands-on experience, collaborate with peers, and explore real-world applications of SAP's latest innovations in Customer Experience, Business AI, and Commerce. 
 Our team ( Fernando Redondo , Deepali Johnson , and Cui Dr. Jian ) was fortunate to contribute through two Pre-Conference Trainings (PCTs) and two Hands-On Labs (HOLs), each designed to help attendees move beyond theory and into practical execution. 
 Pre-Conference Trainings: Deep Learning Through Interaction 
 This year, our team of three instructors delivered two four-hour Pre-Conference Trainings: 
 Building Autonomous CX Workflows with SAP Business AI and Joule 
 Autonomous CX Deep Dive: Lead-to-Fulfillment Processes 

 Each PCT welcomed fewer than ten participants, creating an ideal environment for discussion, collaboration, and personalized coaching. The small group format allowed us to go much deeper into the topics than would be possible in a traditional conference session. 
 Over four hours, participants worked through numerous demonstrations, guided exercises, and practical examples. Rather than simply observing technology in action, attendees had the opportunity to experiment, ask detailed questions, and explore challenges specific to their own organizations. 
 The intimate setting also fostered valuable peer-to-peer conversations. Participants not only learned from the instructors but also from one another, sharing experiences, perspectives, and strategies for driving innovation in customer experience processes. 
 For the instructor team, one of the most rewarding aspects was seeing how quickly the sessions evolved into collaborative workshops where everyone actively contributed to the learning experience. 

 Hands-On Labs: Learning by Doing 
 In addition to the PCTs, we delivered two Hands-On Labs: 
 Enhancing Marketing, Sales, and Service Excellence with Autonomous Agents 
 Duration: 75 minutes 
 Participants: 20 
 Accelerating B2B Commerce with SAP Commerce Cloud 
 Duration: 60 minutes 
 Participants: 16 
 The Hands-On Labs provided a different type of learning experience. While the PCTs emphasized deep exploration and guided instruction, the HOLs focused on participants completing activities independently while receiving real-time support from the team. 
 This format allowed attendees to directly interact with the solutions, navigate scenarios at their own pace, and gain confidence through practical application. Our role was less about presenting and more about enabling success, answering questions, troubleshooting challenges, and helping participants get the most out of each exercise. 

 It was encouraging to see attendees actively engaging with the systems, experimenting with new capabilities, and sharing insights with fellow participants throughout the labs. 
 Why PCTs and HOLs Matter 
 Conference agendas are often packed with keynotes, breakout sessions, and networking opportunities. While these formats provide tremendous value, PCTs and HOLs offer something unique: real experience . 
 Both training formats give participants dedicated time to: 
 Apply concepts in realistic scenarios. 
 Gain hands-on experience with SAP CX solutions. 
 Ask detailed questions and receive immediate feedback. 
 Exchange ideas with peers facing similar business challenges. 
 Build and strengthen their professional networks. 
 For many attendees, these sessions become some of the most memorable and valuable aspects of the event because they transform learning into action. 

 A Great Experience for Participants and Instructors 
 Looking back, what made these sessions successful was not just the content but the interaction. The smaller groups in the PCTs created highly engaging conversations, while the larger HOL audiences brought energy and diverse perspectives to every exercise. 
 Together, we had the opportunity to connect with more than 50 professionals who invested their time to deepen their knowledge of autonomous customer experience processes, SAP Business AI, Joule, and SAP Commerce Cloud. 
 We would like to thank every participant who joined us, asked challenging questions, shared experiences, and helped create such an engaging learning environment. 
 Looking Ahead to 2027 
 As a team, we leave Las Vegas energized by the positive feedback and the enthusiasm we saw throughout the week. Our biggest challenge for next year is clear: offer more sessions and reach a broader audience . 
 The demand for practical, hands-on learning continues to grow, particularly around autonomous agents, AI-powered business processes, and end-to-end customer experience transformation. We are already exploring ways to expand our portfolio of training sessions and labs to provide even more opportunities for attendees to gain real-world experience. 
 If SAP Connect 2026 confirmed one thing, it is that participants want more than presentations. They want to build, experiment, learn from peers, and leave with skills they can immediately apply. 
 We're excited to continue that journey and look forward to seeing even more of you next year. See you at SAP Connect 2027! 🚀

title: Implementing Mass Approval for SRM Documents via OData Batch/Changeset Processing
author: mithiljain
text:
I recently built a unified approval inbox for SRM documents — one Fiori-style screen where an approver could see everything waiting on them across document types and approve or reject in bulk, instead of opening each document individually. The single-item approve/reject case wasn't the hard part; SRM has well-documented workflow decision APIs for that. What actually took real design thinking was the mass approval case — a user selecting twenty items and hitting "Approve" once, and expecting all twenty to process together, with individual success/failure feedback per item, and the whole batch to roll back cleanly if something needed re-doing. 
 That's fundamentally an OData $batch / changeset processing problem , not a workflow problem, and it's the part I couldn't find much practical guidance on specifically for SRM. There's a good generic write-up on SAP Community covering the mechanics of CHANGESET_BEGIN / CHANGESET_PROCESS / CHANGESET_END for OData batch requests in general — but nothing that walks through applying it to an actual SRM mass-workflow-decision scenario, where you're not just creating header/item entities, you're driving /SAPSRM/FU_WF_RFC_DECISION per work item inside that changeset loop. title: SAP RAR Transformation from CIP to OIP: Architecture Evolution, SD Integration, and Implementation
author: Purushottam_Arote
text:
🚀 SAP S/4HANA RAR: Transforming Classic Inbound Processing (CIP) to Optimized Inbound Processing (OIP) 

 Recently, I had the opportunity to work on a CIP-to-OIP transformation for a business process integrated with SAP SD and SAP Revenue Accounting and Reporting (RAR). 

 🎯 The objective: Move from the traditional CIP model to real-time processing while minimizing the impact on existing business processes. 

 In this blog, I share my hands-on experience implementing OIP for business process integrated with SAP SD and SAP RAR. 
 I highlight the below key aspects: 🏗 ️ Architecture changes and processing flow 
 ⚙️ Key differences between CIP and OIP 
 🗄 ️ Database impacts 
 🔧 Enhancement adjustments 
 📊 Monitoring differences 
 ✅ Implementation challenges and lessons learned The blog should help SAP RAR consultants, architects, and developers understand what changes, what remains unchanged, and what should be considered before starting an OIP implementation. OIP processes Revenue Accounting Items synchronously and eliminates the traditional transfer and processing job framework used in CIP. Introduction 
 With SAP S/4HANA, SAP introduced Optimized Contract Management (OCM) and Optimized Inbound Processing (OIP) to simplify and modernize Revenue Accounting and Reporting (RAR). OIP represents a fundamental shift in how Revenue Accounting Items (RAIs) are created and processed. Instead of relying on queues and batch jobs, OIP processes RAIs in real time during document creation. SAP positions OIP as the optimized successor to Classic Inbound Processing (CIP) within modern S/4HANA RAR landscapes. 
 Optimized Inbound Processing (OIP) is one of the most significant innovations introduced in S/4 HANA SAP Revenue Accounting and Reporting (RAR). Unlike Classic Inbound Processing (CIP), which relies on background jobs and multi-step processing, OIP enables real-time creation and processing of Revenue Accounting Items (RAIs) directly when operational documents are posted. 
 This article summarizes the key findings from the implementation project. 
 Understanding the Existing CIP Architecture 
 In the traditional CIP architecture, Revenue Accounting Item processing occurs in multiple stages: 
 Sales Order (RAR Relevant) is created 
 SD Billing Document is created. 
 RAI is generated in Raw or Processable status . 
 Program FARR_RAI_TRANSFER converts Raw RAIs to Processable RAIs. 
 Program FARR_RAI_PROC processes the RAI. 
 Revenue Accounting Contracts and POBs are created in OCM. 
 Revenue Recognition and GL postings are executed. 
 This architecture introduces a processing delay because RAIs depend on scheduled background jobs before becoming available for Revenue Accounting processing. The user must also monitor transfer and processing jobs, adding operational overhead. Revenue Accounting inbound processing traditionally uses processing statuses and monitoring frameworks for RAI lifecycle management. 
 What Changes with OIP? 
 The biggest difference is that OIP processes RAIs synchronously. 
 OIP is SAP's new real-time method for creating Revenue Accounting Items (RAIs) inside SAP RAR (Revenue Accounting and Reporting). 
 When an SD Billing document is saved, RAIs are immediately processed without requiring: 
 FARR_RAI_TRANSFER 
 FARR_RAI_PROC 
 Scheduled batch jobs 
 Queue-based intermediate processing 
 The flow becomes: 
 SD Sales Order → SD Billing Document → Processed RAI → Revenue Accounting Contract → Revenue Recognition 
 This significantly reduces latency between the operational transaction and Revenue Accounting processing. Instead of waiting for background jobs, contract creation and downstream processing can start instantly. 
 Key Architecture Changes 
 Before (CIP) 
 Two-step processing model 
 Queue and batch job dependent 
 Multiple RAI status transitions 
 Monitoring via FARR_RAI_MON 
 Legacy /1RA/* tables 
 After (OIP) 
 Single-step real-time processing 
 No transfer job required 
 Immediate Revenue Contract creation 
 Monitoring through Fiori application " Manage Revenue Accounting Items" 
 New FARR_D_* table framework 
 The simplification is not only technical but also operational. Support teams no longer need to monitor multiple inbound processing jobs throughout the day. 
 Changes in RAI Status Management 
 One important behavioral change is the RAI status model. 
 CIP Status Flow 
 Raw → Processable → Processed 
 OIP Status Flow 
 Processed 
 or 
 Postponed → Processed 
 In OIP, if required information is unavailable during processing, the RAI is placed in Postponed status rather than remaining in intermediary technical statuses. Once the missing information is provided, the RAI can be reprocessed. 
 This results in a significantly cleaner operational model. 
 Database Table Changes 
 One of the most important technical impacts of OIP is the replacement of classic RAI tables. 

 For organizations with custom reports, CDS views, custom transactions, or direct table reads, this is often the most significant migration activity because all table dependencies must be reviewed and redesigned. 
 Monitoring and Error Handling After OIP 
 The operational support model also changes. 
 CIP Monitoring 
 FARR_RAI_MON - Revenue Accounting Item Monitor 
 Transfer job monitoring (FARR_RAI_TRANS - Transfer RAI's from Raw (0) to Processable (2) ) 
 Processing job monitoring (FARR_RAI_PROC - Process Revenue Accounting Items) 
 OIP Monitoring 
 Fiori App: Manage Revenue Accounting Items 
 Postponed Revenue Accounting Item processing (Transaction code: FARR_REPR_PPRAI - Reprocess Postponed RAI ) 
 Real-time status visibility 
 The monitoring experience becomes much more business-friendly because users can directly analyze and reprocess postponed items without depending heavily on technical batch-job execution. 
 Lessons Learned 
 1. Mixed CIP and OIP scenarios require significantly more custom code adaptation than initially expected 
 One assumption we made at the beginning was that the transition effort would primarily focus on replacing CIP-specific objects with their OIP equivalents. In reality, the biggest challenge was supporting business processes that relied on extensive custom logic while keeping some processes on CIP and others on OIP during the transition period. This created additional complexity in custom programs, enhancements, and reports. 
 For example, several custom reports were built on legacy Revenue Accounting tables such as /1RA * tables and had to be redesigned to consume the new FARR_D * data model because a simple table replacement was not sufficient. If we were to repeat the project, we would perform a more detailed dependency analysis of custom developments at the very beginning and identify mixed CIP/OIP process impacts before defining the migration approach. 
 2. End-user readiness for the new monitoring approach was more critical than anticipated 
 We initially focused on the technical migration activities and underestimated the impact of changes to daily business operations. With OIP, users can no longer rely on transaction FARR_RAI_MON , which many support and business users used to quickly identify Revenue Accounting Items and navigate to contracts. Instead, they must work with the Fiori app Manage Revenue Accounting Items , where accessing related contracts often requires additional navigation steps through hyperlinks. 
 This change affected troubleshooting efficiency immediately after go-live. Looking back, we would introduce hands-on training and updated support procedures much earlier in the project to ensure users are comfortable with the new Fiori-based monitoring process before the cutover.

 Conclusion 
 Optimized Inbound Processing (OIP) is more than a technical upgrade. It fundamentally changes how operational transactions enter SAP Revenue Accounting and Reporting by replacing batch-oriented processing with real-time Revenue Accounting Item creation and processing. 
 From my implementation experience, the biggest benefits were: 
 Real-time Revenue Accounting processing 
 Simplified operations 
 Reduced batch-job dependency 
 Improved monitoring through Fiori applications 
 Faster issue resolution 
 However, organizations should carefully assess custom developments, enhancement implementations, and reporting dependencies before migrating from CIP to OIP. 
 For customers already using OCM, OIP is a natural next step toward a fully optimized SAP RAR architecture.

title: SAP PP/DS: Understanding Firming in Production Planning
author: behram581
text:
1. Introduction 

 In SAP Production Planning and Detailed Scheduling (PP/DS), firming is used to protect selected planning elements from automatic changes during planning runs. 

 During production planning, the system may reschedule or modify planned orders to respond to changing demand, material availability, and capacity constraints. Firming helps the planner retain control over selected planning decisions. 

 2. What Is Firming? 

 Firming is a mechanism that restricts changes to planning elements during planning activities, depending on the applicable firming settings and planning process. 

 It is particularly important when planners want to preserve an agreed production plan while allowing the system to continue planning other orders and requirements. 

 3. Why Is Firming Required? 

 Firming helps to: 

 1. Protect selected planned orders from unwanted changes. 

 2. Stabilize the production schedule after planning decisions have been made. 

 3. Support coordination between material availability, production capacity, and delivery commitments. 

 4. Reduce unnecessary rescheduling of orders that are already agreed upon or prepared for execution. 

 5. How Does Firming Work in SAP PP/DS? 

 The system determines how planning elements are treated based on their firming status and the relevant planning settings. 

 For example, a planned order may be firmed after the planner has reviewed its production dates and confirmed material availability. 

 During subsequent planning runs, the firming settings influence whether the system can change the order or its scheduling details. 

 The exact behavior depends on the planning element, firming mechanism, planning procedure, and configuration. 

 5. Firming and the Planning Time Fence 

 The planning time fence is an important concept in production planning. 

 It defines a period within which planning changes are restricted according to the applicable settings. Firming, however, is not the same as the planning time fence. 

 A planning time fence controls planning behavior within a defined time horizon, whereas firming can protect specific planning elements according to the relevant firming rules. 

 6. Practical Business Scenario 

 Consider a manufacturing company producing industrial pumps. 

 The planner creates planned orders for the next two weeks. After reviewing component availability, machine capacity, and customer delivery dates, the planner decides to firm selected orders. 

 When a subsequent planning run is executed, the firming settings help protect those selected orders while the system continues to plan other requirements. 

 This supports a more controlled and stable production planning process.

title: What's New in the SAP SuccessFactors App for Microsoft Teams — 2H 2026 Release
author: sarahhu
text:
Bringing HR into the flow of work is at the heart of what we do with the SAP SuccessFactors app for Microsoft Teams . Instead of switching tools, employees and managers can handle their day-to-day HR tasks — requesting time off, giving feedback, acting on approvals and goals — right where they already collaborate, inside Microsoft Teams. 
 Here's an overall feature highlight with a short demo recording in case you are not familar with this whole solution - E2E flow demo recording 
 With the 2H 2026 release , we've shipped a set of enhancements focused on transparency, flexibility, and a smoother everyday experience. Here are the highlights: 
 🗓 ️ See the real impact before you submit — Deduction on Request Time Off 
 The Request Time Off quick action now shows a dedicated Deduction field alongside the requested duration. Employees see exactly how much will be deducted from their time account — separate from what they request — so there are no surprises, fewer mistakes, and fewer follow-ups with HR. This is especially helpful for complex leave scenarios where the deduction differs from the requested duration. 

 💬 A better Continuous Feedback experience 
 Requesting and giving feedback is now clearer and more flexible: the topic is split into Topic Name and Topic Description , users can add up to three questions (or remove the ones they don't need), and when a request originates from the SuccessFactors activity list, the related activity and its linked goals are shown right in Teams. Messages referencing "activity" or "goal" can also be customized. 

 🔐 Simpler permissions — Feature-Level Consent for Calendar Sync 
 Admins can now grant the required permissions on behalf of users. Once consent is in place, people can sync absences and holidays to their calendars without going through a separate consent flow each time — one less step, a smoother experience. 

 ✏️ More message customization 
 We've expanded customization across more quick actions and notifications — including Manage My Cases , Sync Absences/Holidays to Calendar , and Delegate My Workflows (toggle labels, section headings, delegation options, field labels, and more). Tailor the wording to your organization's terminology and tone. 

 ✅ Mark Goal as Complete — now as a notification and in the Home Tab 
 Employees get timely notifications and can act on goals that are approaching their due date or overdue, directly in Teams. If a goal isn't completed yet, it stays in the Home Tab → To-Do section — consistent with the SAP SuccessFactors Home Page experience. 

 A couple of things customers often ask: 
 Can I customize the app's name and logo? Yes — the app name and icon can be customized through the Teams Admin Center (see Microsoft's documentation). 
 Do you support multiple tenants? One SuccessFactors tenant → multiple Microsoft tenants is supported today , configurable directly in the Work Tech configuration. Multiple SuccessFactors tenants → one Microsoft tenant is in progress , targeted for later this year.

title: Defining UDV for Horizontal Fields
author: OferOz
text:
The latest version of SAP Business One Web Client 10.0 FP 2608 introduces a powerful enhancement to User-Defined Values : you can now assign a UDV to a specific field even when multiple fields share the same label. 
 Background: In SAP Business One Web Client, it's common for two or more controls to sit under a single label or section header – for example, Email and Fax checkboxes in Business Partner form. Until now, if you wanted to assign a UDV to one of those fields, it was not possible since the system couldn't clearly indicate which field had the assignment – the orange brackets [] used as the UDV indicator were placed at the label level, so when multiple fields shared that label, there was no way to tell which one was actually linked to a UDV. 
 To fully support such case, we redesigned the indicator. The orange brackets have been replaced with a dedicated new icon – a standard Fiori icon that intuitively signals a value has been customized by the user. 
 With this new icon design: 
 - The icon is placed next to each individual field, not at the label level 
 - In object edit mode, the icon appears as greyed-out, serving as a non-interactive visual indicator that the field is linked to a UDV 
 - In UDV edit mode, the same icon turns blue, indicating it's clickable, so you can access and modify the UDV definition 
 Example: 
 When you enter Business Partner Edit mode, you will see the following icons appearance : 

 The ‘Sales Employees’ field as well as ‘Email’ and ‘Fax’ checkboxes are defined with UDV. 
 When you enter UDV Edit mode, you will see the following icons appearance: 

 Since 'Remarks' has no UDV defined yet, you’ll see a special icon, blue pencil, so when clicking it, you can create a UDV for it. 
 You can toggle the UDV indicator visibility in your user profile settings under the Display UDV Indicator option. 
 Note that this switch applies only for Edit mode – no indication in View mode.

text:
Hi all, 
 For roughly three weeks we have been unable to reliably deploy any SAP Build Process Automation project. An incident is open with SAP support but has not progressed, so I am posting here in case others are seeing the same behavior or know of a workaround. 
 ERROR 
 When deploying any project, the deployment fails with: 
 "The project (ID: <project id>, version: X.Y.Z) in the environment (ID: <env>) could not be deployed." 
 More details: "Errors occurred while deploying an artifact to a runtime. (component: Integration Gateway)" 
 Followed by a list of: "Compilation failed for project <project id>: Request failed with status code 500" 
 The listed projects are unrelated to the one being deployed. The error enumerates many other projects in the tenant, all failing compilation at the same time with the same 500. 
 In one case the dialog itself stated: "An error occurred in the Integration Gateway during agent compilation. Please use the Copy Error Details button to copy the error information and include it when opening a support ticket (SNOW)." 
 WHAT WE HAVE ALREADY RULED OUT 
 - Not specific to one project: fails on several existing projects deployed in isolation. 
 - Not specific to project content: fails on a brand-new project containing a single trivial Condition step. 
 - Not specific to Joule Studio: fails equally on a plain Process Automation project with no Skill or Joule artifact. 
 - Not specific to one environment: reproduced in both a Shared Environment and a Private Environment. 
 - Not specific to deployment: the same failure occurs when running Test. 
 - Not specific to region: we created a brand-new subaccount in EU10 and the failure reproduces there as well. 
 - Not an Agent version issue: Agent version 3.44. 
 - Design Console reports 0 errors in all cases. 
 OBSERVED PATTERN

title: Prone to errors: VALUE #( BASE itab ( comp99 = 3 ) )
author: Sandra_Rossi
text:
This doesn't fill the component COMP99 of all lines of ITAB2: REPORT zdemo.
TYPES:
 BEGIN OF ty_line,
 a TYPE i,
 comp99 TYPE i,
 END OF ty_line.
TYPES ty_itab TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_line WITH EMPTY KEY.
DATA(itab) = VALUE ty_itab( ( a = 1 ) ( a = 2 ) ).
DATA(itab2) = VALUE ty_itab( BASE itab ( comp99 = 3 ) ). 
 Why? How to do? 
 Thanks. 
 Sandra 
 ANSWER: 
 I admit that anyone could get into the trap, including me. If I remember well, I had already posted on the same topic in the forum years ago. 
 When using structures, that works as expected: DATA(structure) = VALUE ty_line( a = 1 ).
DATA(structure_2) = VALUE ty_line( BASE structure comp99 = 3 ). 
 Trying the same kind of syntax for an internal table leads to a syntax error: DATA(itab2) = VALUE ty_itab( BASE itab comp99 = 3 ). 
 If trying with parentheses, there's no syntax error anymore: DATA(itab2) = VALUE ty_itab( BASE itab ( comp99 = 3 ) ). 
 Alas, it has a different meaning: 
 It means that the internal table is copied as is, and a new line is added with COMP99 = 3 (and the other components have initial values). 
 Instead, do as follows: DATA(itab2) = VALUE ty_itab( FOR <line > IN itab
 ( VALUE #( BASE <line> comp99 = 3 ) ) ). 
 or the old way: DATA(itab2) = itab.
MODIFY itab2 FROM VALUE #( comp99 = 3 ) TRANSPORTING comp99 WHERE comp99 <> 3. 
 Sandra

title: Fast-Growth Companies Have the Biggest AI Opportunity, Few Are Capturing It
author: Santina Franchi
text:
Artificial intelligence has become one of the fastest-adopted technologies in business history. As a result, AI has become ubiquitous. AI value, however, hasn’t. 
 Run your business on an AI cloud ERP built for companies of any size 

 Learn how 

 SAP’s latest global research with Oxford Economics reveals that organizations are already using AI across approximately 25% of business tasks , yet despite this momentum, only nine percent of organizations have fundamentally adapted their business around AI. 

 That gap matters. It suggests that while AI adoption is accelerating, most companies are not embedding it into how the business actually operates. 

 This is precisely the challenge the Autonomous Enterprise is designed to solve: moving AI beyond individual productivity gains to orchestrating end-to-end business processes and delivering value across the enterprise. 

 “Conversations with clients have fundamentally shifted. Customers are no longer asking about how to deploy AI, they’re demanding ways to harness it rapidly and to scale it to unlock maximum business value while minimizing risk,” explained DK Sinha, CEO of Accenture Edge. “Programs like ADVANCE are built exactly for that: combining standardized delivery, unrivaled industry expertise, and AI-enabled accelerators to help organizations capture the full potential of their transformation. The result is greater speed, predictability, and confidence as they build their digital core and reinvent with AI.” 

 SAP often describes the Autonomous Enterprise as AI built on data, processes, and governance. That sequence is important. Research consistently shows that poor data quality remains one of the biggest obstacles to enterprise AI, and mission-critical business processes cannot be “almost right.” AI needs the same controls, auditability, and compliance that organizations already expect from their ERP systems. 

 Why do so many AI initiatives stall? 

 The Oxford Economics findings point to an important conclusion: the biggest obstacle is no longer AI technology, it is business readiness. 

 Many organizations have added AI to individual applications. Far fewer have transformed their businesses to connect AI to the information, processes, and governance needed to create enterprise-wide value and move from piecemeal to enterprise-wide AI: 

 That distinction explains why so many pilots struggle to scale. 

 “AI can only support intelligent business decisions when it is grounded in how the business operates, including who the customer is, which contract applies, what inventory is available, which approval policies are in place, and which regulatory requirements must be met,” said Javier Navarro, SAP global head at SEIDOR. “As a trusted SAP partner, our role is to help clients connect AI to the data, processes, and governance that enable real business value.” 

 Most AI knows natural language. Enterprise AI must know the language of your business. This is the difference between using AI and running an AI-powered business, one where humans and AI work together across the enterprise, with AI grounded in trusted business data, governed processes, and enterprise-grade controls to deliver accurate, secure, and compliant outcomes for better and faster decision-making. 

 Medium-sized fast-growth companies have the greatest opportunity 

 Fast-growth companies are in a unique position: they have the agility to move faster than large enterprises, yet they still have the scale to generate meaningful value from AI. These businesses have unique competitive advantages, including fewer systems to integrate, shorter decision-making chains, less technical debt, and typically more willingness to adopt modern, cloud-native platforms. Autonomous enterprise capabilities represent a unique opportunity for these businesses to punch above their size. 

 This means they can deploy autonomous capabilities in weeks, not years, and see ROI far more quickly, turning agility into a genuine growth advantage against slower competitors. 

 SAP’s Autonomous Enterprise strategy is designed precisely for this reality. It provides AI agents with a structured understanding of business entities, relationships, and processes—giving them the context needed to support real business execution. 

 Realizing that value, however, also requires rethinking how business transformation itself is delivered to fast-growth companies that are focused on fast outcomes. 

 The most challenging part is not implementing AI technology, but redesigning the operating model to eliminate dependency on consultants and put more power in the hands of the customer. Traditionally, transformation was designed around consultant-driven delivery, resulting in high costs, long timelines, and knowledge dependence. We challenged this model based on three principles: customer enablement-first, customer ownership, and AI-driven continuous learning. 

 “AI allows us to build knowledge directly into the organization through each stage of the transformation journey,” said Jiro Furuya, CEO, Freedom Consulting. “At the customer level, AI provides real-time guidance and support for day-to-day operations; at the consultant level, tools such as SAP Joule for Consultants enhance problem-solving and accelerate deliver; and underneath, a centralized data foundation continuously learns from every project, ensuring that knowledge compounds over time. This model and SAP GROW Fast methodology allow us to deliver go-lives in six-week waves, significantly accelerating time-to-value while ensuring that capability stays within the customer organization.” 

 The power of ecosystem 

 Clearly, no company becomes an Autonomous Enterprise alone. Technology alone doesn’t create an Autonomous Enterprise—business transformation does. And while SAP provides the trusted platform, our rich ecosystem of partners translates the capabilities into measurable business outcomes. 

 Partners bring the industry expertise, business process knowledge, and change management capabilities to help customers identify the highest-value use cases, integrate SAP with the broader IT landscape, develop industry-specific AI agents, and accelerate adoption—turning the promise of AI into enterprise-wide value much faster than companies could achieve on their own. 

 As a result, SAP has launched a €100 million partner fund to accelerate customer adoption of AI assistants and agents, recognizing that innovation at scale requires a vibrant ecosystem. For fast-growing companies, this dramatically lowers the barrier to adoption. 

 The first chapter of AI was about helping people work faster. The next chapter is about helping businesses think, decide, and operate more intelligently. That is the promise of the Autonomous Enterprise. 

 Becoming an Autonomous Enterprise is not just about AI itself, but about bringing together SAP, partners, and transformation expertise to accelerate outcomes. For fast-growth companies, this is an opportunity to compete differently, scale more intelligently, and define the next generation of market leaders. 

 Santina Franchi is president of the SAP Corporate Segment.
